# Source-derived Kotlin/JVM voice policy variant

**Research only. No protected repair, device action, production merge or Phase 2 closure.**

The exploratory Hunter reads a bounded inventory of 66 original JARVIS Kotlin
sources from commit `747c14b5d97750a7b2736968e2d516f02448558d`, validating each
source against its local Git blob. It discovers one policy method and its
cross-file caller and extracts guarded action words from the original Kotlin
regex rather than receiving a failing input or a hardcoded suspect filename.

The generator produces metamorphic punctuation variants of direct operational
requests and independent benign explanatory questions. An original-source
Kotlin/JVM oracle executes the actual `OfflineVoiceQuestionGate` and
`LocalGgufPolicy` together for every generated case. Original acceptance of
punctuation-mutated operational requests is RED; the guarded candidate
normalizes punctuation and must accept none (GREEN). A deliberately incorrect
candidate rejecting all questions must fail benign-control verification.

The temporary Fixer draft is pinned to the original policy's commit and Git
blob. It is a narrow rule-specific transformation, not a generalized Fixer.
The isolated runner compiles all three Kotlin variants with Kotlin 2.0.21,
runs original JVM oracles, checks a disposable local Judge plan and exact
rollback against a Git tree, and leaves JARVIS untouched.

CI runs inside Bubblewrap with an enforced AppArmor profile, no network, and
requires >=90% line and branch coverage for the new Hunter and Fixer modules.

## Interpretation boundaries

This is an *unregistered variant* in a previously known read-only voice
policy family. It demonstrates two-file behavioral interaction, not a
novel family, general Kotlin compiler-proven causality, generalized Fixer
or discovery of a 3+ file causal chain. A read-only classifier admitting a
command as a QUESTION does not execute that command: the system explicitly
preserves `canIssueDeviceActions=false`. The experiment is not an Android
device test or authorization to change the product.
